chunks: From him, from Abī ʿAbdillāh, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from ʿAlī عليه السلام, who said:
There is no hadd punishment upon an insane person until he regains consciousness, nor upon a child until he reaches understanding, nor upon a sleeping person until he wakes.

key_terms.النَّائِمِ: a sleeping person not presently conscious
key_terms.حَدٌّ: a fixed legal punishment prescribed under Islamic law
key_terms.صَبِيٍّ: a child not yet legally accountable
key_terms.مَجْنُونٍ: an insane person who lacks sound awareness
key_terms.يُدْرِكَ: to attain understanding or legal maturity

ai.seo_question: When are hadd punishments lifted from a person in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith states that legal hadd punishments do not apply to those who lack conscious legal responsibility: the insane person until recovery, the child until maturity or discernment, and the sleeper until awakening. It expresses a foundational principle in Islamic jurisprudence that accountability depends upon awareness and capacity.
